name: Premier Energies Ltd
title: Premier Energies Ltd - 544238 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Premier Energies' cell and module capacity heads to 16.75 GW by July 2026 with a ₹5,100 crore FY27 capex plan, while management declined to guide on margins despite rising cell and silver costs.

summary.headline: Premier Energies FY26 revenue rose 20.7% to INR8,026 crore and PAT 61.1% to INR1,510 crore, with order book at INR14,010 crore (+66% YoY).
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue of INR8,026 crore (+20.7% YoY) and PAT of INR1,510 crore (+61.1% YoY), with operational EBITDA margin of 30.4% and PAT margin of 18.8%. The 5.6 GW Sitarampur module plant is complete and expected to reach full ramp-up in about two months, and the Transcon 51% acquisition is closed. Capacity is set to rise to 16.75 GW by July 2026, with FY27 capex of INR5,100 crore. Management guided to no specific margin numbers, citing rising cell, silver and freight costs, and said it would pass silver risk to customers on new orders. The K-Solar acquisition was dropped, and the company is pursuing an inverter JV with SMA SGS as first preference.

segments.name: Cells
segments.commentary: TOPCon cell line commissioned June 2025 is running at 90%+ utilisation; average TOPCon efficiency about 25.5%. Cell market pricing stable at 13.5-14 US cents per watt per management. Cell capacity to rise to 10.6 GW shortly, with a 7 GW cell line due in two tranches (4.8 GW June, 2.2 GW September).

segments.name: Modules
segments.commentary: Module capacity 11.1 GW; management says utilisation is about 75% (roughly 7-7.5 GW). The 5.6 GW Sitarampur plant uses about 40% less manpower per MW than existing plants. Management expects DCR share to rise every quarter.

segments.name: Transcon (EPC/transformers, HV/EHV)
segments.commentary: Acquired 51% stake; FY revenue INR423 crore and PAT INR45 crore. Plant due for completion in July 2026; management says it has secured some first orders, and ramp-up is expected to take about two years.

segments.name: Inverters / BESS
segments.commentary: Inverter business pursued via a JV with SMA SGS (first preference) after K-Solar deal lapsed. BESS capacity pace is deliberately slowed due to imports at about 11% duty; localisation policy expected around FY28.

guidance_outlook: Total capacity to rise nearly sevenfold to 16.75 GW by July 2026; management says the 7 GW cell line is on track with no significant delays.
FY27 capex of INR5,100 crore across cells, ingot wafers, batteries and inverters; a roughly INR12,000 crore capex plan is spread over three years from FY26.
More than two-thirds of the INR14,010 crore order book expected to execute in FY27.
Debt-to-equity target about 1 and debt-to-EBITDA about 1.5x or below, while keeping A+ rating.
Management declined to give margin guidance but says the order book is priced consistently with the past 6-12 months and DCR mix should improve margins.
Europe exports expected to grow after the FTA; US cell plans (Heliene JV paused, now reinitiated) under review.
capex_capacity: Sitarampur 5.6 GW module plant completed, full ramp-up expected in about two months.
7 GW cell line capex is about INR3,000 crore and is about 35% below industry benchmark; 4.8 GW due June and 2.2 GW due September, with 4-6 months to stabilise.
A parallel 7 GW Brownfield cell line is possible at 30-40% lower capex, with land and infrastructure available.
Ingot wafer, aluminium frame, battery storage and transformer projects have started.
Module capacity 11.1 GW; cell capacity to 10.6 GW shortly, reaching 16.75 GW total by July 2026.
demand_pricing: FY26 new installations about 45 GW AC (+87% YoY), with total module demand near 60 GW.
About 30 GW of FY26 demand (rooftop, KUSUM, C&I) shifts to domestic cells from June 1 under ALMM-2; utility-scale (about 15 GW) demand is expected around FY28-29 because of grandfathered projects.
Management expects a large DCR order surge once ALMM-2 timing is clear, with the C&I segment (about 15 GW) becoming a major buyer.
Silver cost risk is now passed through to customers on new orders; Zero Busbar cells cut silver use by about 10%.
Management said non-DCR modules are being phased out and DCR share rises every quarter; cell prices in China rose from about 3.5 to 6-6.2 cents per watt, passed through on non-DCR modules.
Management said the ALMM-2 timing risk to the order book is immaterial because C&I deliveries in the current order book fall after October-November.

qa_highlights.question: Did the DCR share of module volume double sequentially, based on the DCR portal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the DCR portal is a verification and traceability tool, not a sales indicator, and that the cell vs DCR module mix changes quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Why did stock purchases rise about four times YoY, and what is the debt-to-equity target?
qa_highlights.answer: Stock build is planned for supply-chain security and the new 5.6 GW line. Net debt rose about INR660 crore for the capex programme; the target is debt-to-equity around 1 and debt-to-EBITDA at or below 1.5x.

qa_highlights.question: Why was K-Solar dropped, and what are the inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: It was a non-binding term sheet; final documentation terms could not be agreed. Management remains committed to inverters and prefers a JV with SMA SGS, to be finalised in the next few months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost trends and the bill of materials change for modules?
qa_highlights.answer: Cell costs rose to about 6-6.2 cents from 3.5 cents, passed through on non-DCR modules. DCR margins are maintained through scale and mix. Glass cost unchanged; aluminium (about 11% of module cost) rose slightly, offset by design changes.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 7 GW line and order book convert?
qa_highlights.answer: Over two-thirds of the INR14,010 crore order book executes in FY27. Some cell orders extend into FY28. Module utilisation is about 75% (7-7.5 GW).

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk to the order book if ALMM-2 is delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no material risk, because C&I orders in the book deliver after October-November and any delay of a quarter would not affect them.

risks_watch: Rising cell, silver, copper and freight costs; management gave no margin guidance.
Net debt rising with capex (INR5,100 crore in FY27); debt-to-EBITDA ceiling of 1.5x.
Timing of ALMM-2 (June 1) and whether the expected DCR order surge arrives.
Ramp of 7 GW cell line (4.8 GW June, 2.2 GW September) and TOPCon efficiency move from 25.5% toward 25.8%, which management expects takes a couple of quarters.
Transcon plant completion (July 2026) and certification (6-12 months).
US and Europe expansion timing, and the BESS localisation policy (management: 3-4 months, possibly first half of FY27).
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, scale and the DCR mix, and confident the order book is priced for margins. Evasive on forward margins and on the cell order book's module split, repeatedly declining to quantify. Cautious on utility-scale timing and BESS localisation, and on the K-Solar deal being dropped.
key_quotes: The most pleasing thing about these numbers is that they have been achieved in a challenging overall environment with increase in several commodity prices and freight prices.
We believe this is going to provide a major boost to long-term demand for the sector.
So through this capex cycle our endeavour is to maintain our A plus rating and we want to maintain the debt-to-equity ratio at about 1 and debt-to-EBITDA ratio at about 1.5 or below.
Yes, some costs are going up, but at the same time we are also doing a lot of work behind the scenes to be able to reduce our cost and improve the efficiencies in the overall business.

growth.why: Capacity rises to 16.75 GW by July 2026 with 4.8 GW cell line due June and 2.2 GW September, and a INR14,010 crore order book (+66% YoY) with over two-thirds expected to execute in FY27 backs growth; no explicit revenue growth guidance was given, and management declined margin guidance.
